solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This clue isn't a liger, for example

parts.note: a liger is a cross between a lion and a tigress, an example of a hybrid

explanation.surface: A puzzle-maker insists this particular clue is no hybrid big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: this is a Down clue, so it is not the other direction. A liger is a lion-tiger hybrid, hence a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Clues run in one of two directions; this one is a Down clue, so it is precisely not the other kind.

clue.text: English drinker, man hard to understand

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
Eric stands for any man's name

explanation.surface: An English boozer is described as a man nobody can make sense of.
explanation.definitionFit: Something esoteric is obscure, understood only by a small circle of initiates.

clue.text: Canadian province not welcoming Da Gama on main route going north

indicators.note: the word for not opens up to take in the explorer's first name, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese navigator who reached India by sea

indicators.note: in a Down clue, going north means the piece is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written here with the 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Canadian province refuses to admit a famous explorer travelling north along a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; its digit 1 stands in for the letter I. 'on' simply places that piece below NO(VASCO)T in the Down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of Canada's Atlantic Maritime provinces, with Halifax as its capital.

clue.text: Horse pistol

definitions.meaning: a young male horse is so called
Samuel ... revolver gave its maker's name to a type of handgun

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a young stallion and, from its maker's name, a revolver.

clue.text: Quite quickly, line taken over bird's piercing voice

indicators.note: the line and bird together pierce, or go into, the singing voice

parts.note: alto is a singing voice in the lower female or high male range

indicators.note: in a Down clue, taken over means the line sits above the bird

parts.note: an egret is a white heron; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone quickly notes a line hovering above a bird whose cry is piercing.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning moderately fast, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Beam, extra short

indicators.note: the synonym for extra is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: spare as an adjective means extra, surplus

explanation.surface: A carpenter has a beam that is going to waste, though a bit too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter E from SPARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole or beam, such as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: Spinner given a rest

definitions.meaning: a creature that spins a web
in snooker, the cue rest with a raised arched head is called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: Snooker players use a raised cue rest with legs to reach over a ball; it shares its name with the web-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The arachnid spins silk, and snooker's raised rest is named after it for its many legs.

clue.text: Load of rot, good gracious, cutting fish

indicators.note: the exclamation cuts into the fish, splitting it

parts.note: fry are young fish
lumme is a dated British exclamation of surprise, like good gracious

explanation.surface: Exclaiming in surprise at a load of nonsense about filleting fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Flummery is empty flattery or nonsense, as well as a sweet pudding.

clue.text: Purgative, one litre by old Cuban bottles

indicators.note: the Cuban leader's name contains, as a bottle does, the abbreviation for old

parts.note: Fidel Castro was Cuba's revolutionary leader
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old Cuban stockpiling bottles of laxative by the litre.
explanation.definitionFit: This oil from the castor bean was long given as a laxative to clear the bowels.

clue.text: Student, bit of a looker

definitions.meaning: a learner taught by a teacher
the dark opening at the centre of the eye, part of what looks

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a schoolchild being taught and the dark aperture in the iris of the eye.

clue.text: Survive, like the tenth man back in the pavilion?

definitions.meaning: to live or last longer than another

definitions.text: like the tenth man back in the pavilion?
definitions.meaning: the tenth batsman dismissed in cricket ends the innings, being the final one dismissed

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the innings ends when the tenth batsman is dismissed and walks back to the pavilion (the clubhouse); he is the last one out.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlive someone is to continue existing longer than they do.

clue.text: Countess's estate rarely missing leadership without a king

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the trimmed word lies outside the pair
the synonym for rarely loses its first, leading, letter

parts.note: seldom means rarely
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A countess's property is rarely without leadership, lacking any king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing leadership' drops S from SELDOM, leaving ELDOM, which goes 'without' (around) A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A countess is the wife of an earl, whose rank and lands are his earldom.

clue.text: Title among knights I respect

indicators.note: the letters sit among the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A respectful honorific is used among the knights I admire.
explanation.definitionFit: The honorific given to a knight or baronet, placed before the forename.

clue.text: America read about fellowship

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Read up on America to learn about its spirit of fellowship.
explanation.definitionFit: Camaraderie is the trust and friendship among comrades, a sense of fellowship.

clue.text: Phoney verrucas froth up, covering end of chin

indicators.note: the reversed pair covers, or wraps round, the final letter of chin
in a Down clue, up means the verrucas and froth together are read from the bottom

parts.note: verrucas are warts on the foot
foam is froth

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A fake remedy makes verrucas froth up so it covers the end of your chin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns WARTSFOAM into MAOFSTRAW, which is 'covering' N, the 'end of' chin.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of straw is a sham figure with no substance, so phoney in nature.

clue.text: Inebriated, Windsor sat in the cellar?

indicators.note: being drunk, the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken Windsor sat in the wine cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: The cellar is below the ground floor, so anyone there is literally on a lower floor of the house.

clue.text: Prowler returned, it's understood

indicators.note: returned says the prowler's word comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a cat prowls at night
the word it, with the 's acting as a link to the definition

explanation.surface: A prowler has come back, and the reason is understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken but implied, so understood without being said.

clue.text: Indication of filthy washer, dark item needing replacement

indicators.note: the letters need replacing, put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A dark garment shows grime, needing to be replaced by a clean one.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'washer' is a person bathing, not a machine: a grimy bather leaves a ring round the tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the ring of dirt left around a bath, or on the skin of someone poorly washed.

clue.text: Egg, but no egghead?

definitions.meaning: an egghead is an intellectual, so its opposite is a fool, a nitwit

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a louse egg and, informally, a nitwit or idiot.

clue.text: Well initially, children's game is fine

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: I spy is a guessing game played by children

explanation.surface: Well, a children's guessing game is fine by me.
explanation.definitionFit: Wispy hair or smoke is thin and fine, like a wisp.

clue.text: Blind (partially), bird as dirty woman

parts.note: a slat is one strip of a Venetian blind, part of it
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A partially sighted bird is likened to an unkempt woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Slattern is a dated term for a slovenly, untidy woman.

clue.text: Tombstone cleaner, say, finding death behind apartment backing onto office

indicators.note: onto places the reversed flat right up against the office
behind places the word for death after the rest

parts.note: a den is a study, a home office

indicators.note: backing says the apartment's word runs backwards

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
a loss is a death, as in a bereavement

explanation.surface: A grave cleaner finds death behind an apartment that backs onto an office.
explanation.walkthrough: Tombstones is slang for large teeth. 'backing' turns FLAT into TALF.
explanation.definitionFit: Tombstones is slang for teeth, and this thread cleans between them.

clue.text: One bag in a state, nearly a ton

indicators.note: the one and bag are placed in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York, a US state
I is the Roman numeral one
to net is to bag, catch

explanation.surface: One bag left in a state weighs almost a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton is slang for a hundred, so a number just short of it.

clue.text: Starts to advance round circle, as this line

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: To advance round a circle you follow its curved line.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curved line, part of a circle's circumference.

clue.text: Touch God in Lewis

indicators.note: the god is set in the author's initials

parts.note: C S Lewis, author of the Narnia books
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: Feeling the hand of God in a Lewis novel.
explanation.walkthrough: C S Lewis wrote overtly Christian works, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle, affectionate stroke or touch.

clue.text: Many near it, building tower in Istanbul, say

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

indicators.note: building means the letters are constructed into a new form

explanation.surface: Many people live near the tall structure being built in Istanbul.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque, many of which rise over Istanbul.

clue.text: Red, though not often spotted

definitions.meaning: of meat, underdone and still red inside

explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is just a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both underdone steak and something seldom encountered.

clue.text: Browner in the direction of flower

parts.note: to means towards, in the direction of
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Something gets browner as it moves towards a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster is a device that browns bread, so it is a browner.

clue.text: Instrument which sounds like a potato?

indicators.note: sounds like says a word is said out loud

parts.note: a potato is a tuber, a swollen underground stem

explanation.surface: An instrument with a name like a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is a large low-pitched brass instrument.

clue.text: To the left, or to the right — it turns!

indicators.text: To the left, or to the right
indicators.note: reading leftwards or rightwards gives the same letters, so the word is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look, left or right, something is spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Waxy substance with which author covers composer, then runs

indicators.note: the author's surname covers, wrapping around, the composer and runs

parts.note: Martin or Kingsley Amis, English novelists

indicators.note: then places the runs after the composer

parts.note: Alban Berg, Austrian composer
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A waxy substance the author smears over a composer before running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy secretion of sperm whales, used in perfume.
